question: If I keep recharging without a gap, how long does my banked data hang around?
expected_answer: Each banked amount expires 56 days after it was banked, even if you keep recharging on time; it doesn't stay indefinitely.

key_facts: Each banked amount expires 56 days after it was banked
even if you keep recharging on time
meta.common_prior: Banked data stays indefinitely, up to the bank limit, as long as you keep recharging before expiry.

question: What's the most banked data I can hold onto on the forty dollar recharge?
expected_answer: The Data Bank limit on the $40 recharge is 100 GB; the higher 200 GB limit applies only to the $50 recharge.

key_facts: The bank limit is 100 GB on the $30 and $40 recharges

question: If I hotspot my laptop off my phone, why does the data go so fast?
expected_answer: Laptops use much more data than phones: they load full desktop websites, run software and system updates, sync cloud folders and stream video at higher resolution, often in the background.

key_facts: laptops run background updates and cloud syncing
laptops load heavier desktop pages and higher-quality video

question: Why am I still being billed when I cancelled my home internet last week?
expected_answer: Since 1 August 2026, home internet and postpaid services require 30 days' notice, so billing continues until the end of the 30-day notice period after you asked to cancel, followed by a final bill.

key_facts: require 30 days' notice
billing continues until the end of the 30-day notice period
meta.common_prior: Billing stops when you cancel; the final bill is pro-rated to the cancellation date.

question: If I switch internet providers, can I keep my old Wi-Fi name and password?
expected_answer: Yes. The Wi-Fi name and password are just settings on your modem, so set the new modem to the same network name, password and security type and your devices will reconnect automatically.
answer_aliases: set the same SSID and password

key_facts: the Wi-Fi name (SSID) and password are settings on the modem
use the same name and password and devices reconnect automatically

question: I'm off to Bali next month, how does the travel pass work over there?
expected_answer: Bali is in Zone 2: the Travel Pass starts automatically the first time you use your phone there on a given day and costs $10 per day, with 1 GB data each day plus unlimited standard calls to Australian numbers and texts.

key_facts: Zone 2 covers Indonesia (including Bali)
A Zone 2 Travel Pass costs $10 per day
Each day includes 1 GB data

question: So if I use it right when I land, when does that day pass end?
expected_answer: A Travel Pass day runs from midnight to midnight Sydney time, not 24 hours from when it starts, so it ends at the next midnight Sydney time.

history.content: I'm landing in Bali around eleven at night on the fifth.
Okay, your travel pass will start automatically the first time you use your phone there.

key_facts: A Travel Pass day runs from midnight to midnight Sydney time, not 24 hours from when it starts
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: It lasts 24 hours from the moment it first activates.

question: I'm off to Bali next month, how do I stop apps racking up roaming charges?
expected_answer: Turn off data roaming (or mobile data) in your phone's settings and use Wi-Fi instead, and switch off automatic app updates, background refresh and photo backup over mobile data.

key_facts: turn off data roaming or mobile data in settings
use Wi-Fi and stop background refresh and auto-updates

question: How does it work if my postpaid bill slips past the due date?
expected_answer: Nothing is added for paying late, because late payment fees aren't charged at all. But if the bill is still unpaid 14 days after the due date, outgoing calls, texts and data are suspended.

key_facts: Tallowood does not charge late payment fees
unpaid 14 days after the due date, we suspend outgoing calls, texts and data
meta.common_prior: A late payment fee of around $10 to $20 is added to the next bill.

question: Um, my direct debit bounced last week, why's there an extra charge on my bill?
expected_answer: A failed direct debit attracts a $7.50 dishonour fee to cover bank processing costs, and the payment is retried 3 days later.

key_facts: a $7.50 dishonour fee applies
we retry the payment 3 days later

question: Um, my direct debit bounced a few days ago, why would the bank reject it?
expected_answer: Usually because there weren't enough funds in the account on the day, or the account or card details changed, the card expired or was replaced, or the bank blocked or limited the debit.
answer_aliases: not enough money in the account

key_facts: insufficient funds on the day
changed, expired or replaced account or card details

question: If I cancel my plan, do I have to pay off the rest of my phone straight away?
expected_answer: No. Phone repayments are separate from the plan, so you can keep paying the phone monthly on the original schedule; the remaining balance does not become due straight away.

key_facts: you can keep paying the phone monthly on the original schedule
the remaining balance does not become due straight away
meta.common_prior: Yes, the remaining device balance becomes payable in full on your final bill when you cancel.

question: I'm still paying off my phone, um, can I upgrade to a new one before the term finishes?
expected_answer: Yes, once you have made 12 monthly repayments: trade in your current phone in working condition and the remaining repayments are waived; without a trade-in you keep paying off the old phone too.
answer_aliases: after twelve months with a trade-in

key_facts: once you have made 12 monthly repayments
trading in your current phone in working condition
we waive the remaining repayments

question: I'm still paying off my phone, um, if it gets stolen, can the thief just use it with their own SIM?
expected_answer: Not on Australian networks once it is reported: carriers share a blocked-device list, so a reported phone's IMEI is blocked and it won't connect with any SIM, although it may still work on Wi-Fi or overseas.
answer_aliases: not once the IMEI is blocked

key_facts: a reported stolen phone's IMEI is blocked across Australian networks
it will not connect with any SIM once blocked

question: On the home hundred plan, what speed should I typically get at night?
expected_answer: Home 100 has a typical evening speed of 88 Mbps, measured between 7 pm and 11 pm when the network is busiest.

key_facts: Home 100 costs $90 per month, with a typical evening speed 88 Mbps
between 7 pm and 11 pm

question: On the home hundred plan, how long should a two gig download take?
expected_answer: At a full 100 Mbps, about 12.5 megabytes a second, a 2 GB download takes roughly 160 seconds, so around three minutes; in practice it's a bit longer depending on the server and your Wi-Fi.

key_facts: about 160 seconds, roughly 3 minutes
100 Mbps is about 12.5 megabytes per second

question: I'm moving house in three weeks, how much notice do you need to move my internet?
expected_answer: At least 10 business days before your move date; relocation is free if the new address can be self-installed, or $99 if a technician is needed.

key_facts: tell us at least 10 business days before your move date
$99 if a technician appointment is needed

question: I'm moving house in a few days, where's the best spot to put my modem?
expected_answer: Somewhere central and raised, out in the open rather than in a cupboard, and away from thick walls, metal, mirrors, fish tanks and microwaves, so the Wi-Fi signal spreads evenly through the home.
answer_aliases: in the middle of the house, up high

key_facts: central, elevated and in the open
away from thick walls, metal and microwaves

question: What does the outage credit on my bill mean, how's it worked out?
expected_answer: It's the service guarantee credit: if a home internet fault you reported isn't fixed within 2 business days, you get $10 per day for each extra day until it's fixed, applied automatically.

key_facts: if a fault you report isn't fixed within 2 business days, we credit $10 per day for each extra day until it is fixed

question: My phone had no signal all weekend, can I get something knocked off my bill?
expected_answer: Not automatically: there are no automatic credits for mobile outages. If a confirmed network outage hit your area for more than 24 hours, you can request a one-off $10 credit within 30 days.

key_facts: there are no automatic credits for mobile network outages
request a one-off $10 credit within 30 days of the outage
more than 24 hours
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you'll automatically get a pro-rata credit for the days you had no service.

question: It just shows SOS only up the top, what does that mean for calling people?
expected_answer: You can only make emergency calls: SOS only means your phone can't reach your own network but can use another carrier's network for emergency calls, so you can still call 000 or 112, but not make normal calls, texts or use data.
answer_aliases: no coverage from your own network

history.content: I'm out camping near the Grampians this weekend.
Okay, you might be in a patchy coverage area out there. What's the phone showing?

key_facts: no connection to your own network
emergency calls only through another network

question: What ID do I need to activate a prepaid SIM on a student visa?
expected_answer: Your foreign passport plus your visa grant number, and an Australian residential or accommodation address; the online check takes about 10 minutes, or you can verify in store with your passport.

key_facts: foreign passport plus your visa grant number
The online check takes about 10 minutes

question: Why do you guys need to see my ID just to activate a prepaid SIM?
expected_answer: Australian law requires every carrier to verify a prepaid customer's identity before the service is activated; it helps police and emergency services and stops anonymous numbers being used for scams and crime.

key_facts: identity checks for prepaid services are required by law
it helps law enforcement and emergency services and deters misuse

question: I've got a new phone, how does moving my eSIM across work with you?
expected_answer: Up to 3 transfers per calendar month in the app, for free; a fourth or later transfer in the same month needs a store visit with photo ID.

key_facts: up to 3 transfers per calendar month
visit a store with photo ID
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: As many times as you like; eSIM transfers are unlimited and free.

question: Okay, but how do I know if that phone supports eSIM at all?
expected_answer: Check the phone's settings for an Add eSIM option under Mobile or Cellular, dial *#06# to see whether it shows an EID number, or look up the model's specs; a second-hand phone also needs to be carrier-unlocked.

history.content: I've just bought a second-hand phone online.
Nice. Are you planning to put your existing number on it?

key_facts: look for an Add eSIM option in settings
an EID shown via *#06# means eSIM support

question: If I close my prepaid account, what happens to the leftover credit on it?
expected_answer: Yes, any unused dollar credit (not plan inclusions or banked data) is refundable on request within 60 days of closing, paid to an Australian bank account, with a minimum refund of $5.

key_facts: Any unused dollar credit
is refundable on request within 60 days of closing
the minimum refund is $5
meta.common_prior: No, unused prepaid credit is non-refundable when you close the service.

question: If I close my prepaid account, what happens to my number, can someone else get it?
expected_answer: Yes, eventually: a closed number is disconnected and, after a quarantine period, returned to the pool and reissued to someone else. To keep it, port it to another provider before closing.

key_facts: closed numbers are recycled after a quarantine period
port the number out first to keep it

question: If I ring you guys on a Sunday, until when is someone there?
expected_answer: Phone support runs 8 am to 6 pm Sydney time on weekends, so until 6 pm on Sunday; live chat in the app is available 24/7.

key_facts: weekends 8 am to 6 pm, Sydney time

question: How long do you guys actually have to sort it out?
expected_answer: Complaints are aimed to be resolved within 10 business days; if more time is needed you'll be told why and given a new date, no more than 20 business days from when you complained.

history.content: I lodged a complaint about my modem a couple of weeks back.
I can see it on your account, it's still open with our resolutions team.

key_facts: We aim to resolve complaints within 10 business days
no more than 20 business days

question: If you guys can't fix my complaint, who else could I take it to?
expected_answer: The Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman, a free and independent dispute-resolution service; it usually expects you to have given your provider a chance to fix the problem first.

key_facts: the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman
free and independent
